thread:
rachel: Observed weird scheduling churn in dedicated-gpu-pool-eu1 starting ~02:14 UTC. Jobs for tenant `sparkle` bounce between warm and main, causing slot fragmentation and increased tail latency for other tenants.
tom: saw it too. scheduler logs show repeated preempt+requeue loop for pods with lots of short lived outbound connections. could be the same noisy-tenant pattern but hitting our scheduler heuristics.
zhang: digging into metrics: node-alloc-util jumps then scheduler drains ~3 nodes, but pods come back and re-schedule elsewhere. Side effect: kube-proxy conntrack entries spike and some nodes hit netfilter conntrack high watermark.
miguel: infra-bot flagged network-threshold-eu1 at 02:18. infra-bot: ALERT netfilter-conntrack-high node-345 (90%).
rachel: Example trace: `sparkle` has a prefetcher that opens 30k short TCPs/min to s3-backend. It doesn't reuse connections. Combined with our ephemeral port reuse policy, we get connection churn + kernel conntrack churn => kube-proxy delays and kubelet eviction flaps.
tom: Short-term mitigation: reduce scheduler aggressiveness for bursting tenants and mark `sparkle` with soft-isolation tag so it lands in fractional slice. That avoids draining whole nodes. Thoughts?
zhang: sounds reasonable. We have fractional slices but current allocation tries to maximize GPU packing, which makes eviction thrash worse. Soft-isolation would force scatter and reduce pod bumping.
miguel: Can we also enable per-node conntrack tuning as emergency? Increase hashsize and timeout for ESTABLISHED to reduce churn. It's kernel-level and safe for 1hr window.
infra-bot: ACTION_CREATED: change-request #4721 - tag tenant sparkle -> soft-isolation; apply conntrack temp-tune to nodes [341..350]. Created by miguel.
oncall: Oncall applying changes now. Will monitor P95 latency and node.eviction_count.
rachel: Socialize to product: ask sparkle to enable keepalives / HTTP/2 multiplexing in SDKs (reduce client-side churn). I'll ping their SE.
tom: Cost note: soft-isolation increases slice overhead ~2-3% capacity loss for eu1 (more fragmentation) but should reduce emergency scaling by large margin. If this becomes frequent, cost to reconfigure scheduler heuristics may be worth it.
zhang: Implemented a short-lived heuristic tweak: if node.eviction_rate > 0.1/min AND conntrack_util > 70% => prefer scatter-on-alloc for incoming dedicated pods. Rolling to canary now.
miguel: Canary looks good in eu1-canary: evictions dropped 78%, P95 latency for small gen requests down from 420ms -> 60ms.
oncall: infra-bot: RESOLVED netfilter-conntrack-high on node-345. Monitoring 30m.
rachel: Follow-ups: 1) permanent scheduler flag for scatter preference under conntrack pressure 2) telemetry: per-tenant new_conn_rate, per-node conntrack_util, and eviction_rate 3) SDK guidance for keepalive pooling 4) cost comparison: soft-isolation overhead vs extra dedicated pools. I'll draft a short memo.
tom: I'll add a small runbook entry "conntrack-induced scheduling churn" to release-war-room and link detection playbooks.
zhang: also open a perf-req to product to explore internal VPC egress for high-churn tenants to bypass NAT/conntrack entirely.
miguel: thanks team. Noting: if we need to scale long term, dedicated proxy fleet (per-tenant) avoids kernel conntrack pressure but adds infra/ops overhead. Put numbers in the memo.
infra-bot: NOTE: auto-escalate to infra-pager if any node.conntrack_util > 92% for >3m.
oncall: closing loop, adding postmortem stub to #postmortems.
